newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-DE SILVA MAKES TEST HISTORY WITH UNBEATEN 100S.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-DE SILVA MAKES TEST HISTORY WITH UNBEATEN 100S.

text.p: Aravinda de Silva became the first batsman in test history to score two unbeaten centuries in one match as Sri Lanka scented victory over Pakistan in the second and final test on Tuesday.
De Silva followed his 138 not out with 103 not out to help power Sri Lanka's second innings to 386 for four declared on the fourth day, setting Pakistan 426 to win the match and series.
Left-arm fast bowler Chaminda Vaas then dispatched openers Rameez Raja for nought and Salim Elahi for 14 to leave Pakistan on 28 for two at the close.
De Silva's batting has dominated the short series in which he has stroked three consecutive hundreds. He hit 168 in the second innings of the drawn first test in Colombo.

He became the third Sri Lankan to score a century in each innings of a test after Duleep Mendis (105 and 105 against India at Madras in 1982-83) and Asanka Gurusinha (119 and 102 against New Zealand at Hamilton in 1990-91).
The platform for de Silva's compelling performance in the second innings was built by openers Sanath Jayasuriya and Russell Arnold, who extended their overnight 102 without loss to 157.
Jayasuriya, who resumed on 61, went on to complete his second test century, scoring 113 in 290 minutes with one six and nine fours.
Arnold contributed his maiden test 50 as they just failed to beat Sri Lanka's first-wicket record of 159 by Sidath Wettimuny and Ravi Ratnayake against India at Kanpur in 1986-87.
After the openers went and Marvan Atapattu was run out for four, de Silva and captain Arjuna Ranatunga punished the depleted Pakistani attack by adding 105 for the fourth wicket off 107 balls.

With the touring side reduced to two specialist bowlers - leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed and off-spinner Saqlain Mushtaq - Ranatunga raced to 66 off 62 balls, hitting Mushtaq Ahmed for two consecutive sixes soon after reaching his half-century.
But the bowler had his revenge when he had the Sri Lankan skipper stumped by stand-in wicketkeeper Salim Elahi. Ranatunga hit three sixes and nine fours.
Sri Lanka closed their second innings 30 minutes after the tea as soon as de Silva completed his second century. He faced 99 balls in a stay of 169 minutes, hitting one six and 11 fours.
